newsitem.title: CHINA: China says crime rate cut by crackdown.
newsitem.headline: China says crime rate cut by crackdown.

text.p: China trumpeted the success of its "strike hard" anti-crime campaign on Wednesday, saying the number of crimes reported to police in the first 10 months of this year fell 3.1 percent from the year-earlier period.

Major crimes were still on the rise, but the growth rate between January and October was 12 percentage points lower than in the same period period last year, the official Xinhua news agency said, quoting Vice-Minister of Public Security Bai Jingfu.
"The rising trend in crime has been effectively controlled by the campaign," Bai said. "A large number of criminal cases have been solved and many criminals put in jail."
He did not give figures. Local media have reported the execution of thousands of criminals since the campaign was launched in April.
Bai conceded that the successes could turn out to be temporary and that the campaign would have to continue.
In 1996, 395 policemen were killed and more than 8,500 wounded in the line of duty, Xinhua said.
Crime was virtually eliminated after the communists came to power in 1949 but it has staged a comeback in the past two decades with the launch of economic reforms.
